clue.text: Refuse what's left when the sugar's been taken away

definitions.meaning: refuse here is the noun, waste matter, as in the fibrous waste of crushed cane

definitions.text: what's left when the sugar's been taken away
definitions.meaning: the dry pulp remaining after sugar cane has been crushed for its juice

explanation.surface: A grim little note on what remains in the bowl after someone has helped themselves to the sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb, but it is the noun: waste, the residue of crushed sugar cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Both halves describe the fibrous residue of sugar cane after juice extraction, used for fuel and paper.

clue.text: Impudent, unlike one with 29

definitions.meaning: 29 across is a veil, so someone without one shows an uncovered face

explanation.surface: Someone is cheeky, quite unlike a person wearing whatever 29 is.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the veil at 29 across: a veiled woman's face is covered, so the opposite has a bare face.
explanation.definitionFit: Shameless and brazen are synonyms; literally the word describes an uncovered face, the opposite of a veiled one.

clue.text: Little Mary's car is GT involved in crash

indicators.note: things involved in a crash are smashed and mixed up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl named Mary has had her sports car wrecked in an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' is old British slang for the stomach (from a J. M. Barrie play), so 'Little Mary's' means belonging to the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang names the stomach Little Mary, so its possessive means relating to the stomach, the adjective's sense.

clue.text: A clear space close to the flight path

definitions.text: A clear space close to the flight path

parts.words: A clear space close to the flight path
parts.note: reads like an airfield zone beside an aircraft route, but the flight is of stairs: the open shaft around which a staircase climbs

explanation.surface: Sounds like an air-traffic rule about keeping ground clear near a runway approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aircraft; here it is a flight of stairs, and the clear space beside it is the open shaft of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical shaft housing a staircase is the open space alongside its flights of steps.

clue.text: You and I detained by Her Majesty — in jug?

indicators.note: something detained by another is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword abbreviation for the Queen
you and I together are we

explanation.surface: Two people find themselves locked up at the Queen's pleasure, in jug (prison slang).
explanation.walkthrough: 'In jug' suggests prison slang, but 'jug' is the definition: a large pitcher. ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wide-mouthed pitcher for water is a classic example of a jug.

clue.text: Slandered the tail end

definitions.meaning: spoke badly of someone behind their back
read as two words, the rear part

explanation.surface: Someone was badmouthed about their hindquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer gives the back bit, a rear part or tail end.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking ill of someone in their absence is the past tense verb's sense; split up it means the rear portion.

clue.text: Those serving drinks could be locked up

definitions.meaning: bar staff stand on the far side of the counter from the drinkers

explanation.surface: Bartenders might find themselves imprisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar staff work at the back of the bar counter; the same phrase means in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Bartenders stand on the far side of their counters; in prison, inmates sit on the inside of cell grilles.

clue.text: Periodical entertainer

definitions.meaning: a magazine issued at regular intervals, here one of strip cartoons
a performer who makes audiences laugh

explanation.surface: A regular publication that is also a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon magazine is a periodical; a stand-up comedian is a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Fight to capture the Ashes resulting in exhaustion?

indicators.note: a fight capturing something holds it within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a boxing bout is a fight
the Ashes trophy in England–Australia cricket is a tiny urn

explanation.surface: A gruelling contest to win the Ashes cricket series leaves the players worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes, the Test cricket series between England and Australia, is played for a small urn said to hold burnt bails.
explanation.definitionFit: Total physical or mental collapse from overwork is another name for severe exhaustion.

clue.text: Mark left in time

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as the word says

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: A simple instruction to leave a mark at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Tide meaning time survives in Eastertide and Yuletide.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy accent over a Spanish n is a diacritic mark.

clue.text: A tyrant redeemed as member of a sect

indicators.note: read as re-deemed, deemed again from the other direction, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a tsar was an autocratic Russian ruler, a byword for tyrant

explanation.surface: A despot saved from his ways and now joined to a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redeemed' turns A TSAR backwards into the answer; the surface wants it to mean saved by faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian, follower of the Jamaican movement venerating Haile Selassie, is shortened this way.

clue.text: Here ample cocktails could be soon gone

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plentiful drinks at a party are quickly downed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktails' reads as drinks but signals the mix of HERE AMPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fleeting lasts only a short while before vanishing.

clue.text: Warning about old city in uproar

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, as something placed about it

parts.note: golfers shout fore as a warning
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An alarm goes up as an ancient city falls into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the golfer's shout of warning; UR is the crossword's favourite ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: A public outcry or commotion is a synonym for uproar.

clue.text: One acted eccentrically to make a good story

indicators.note: acting eccentrically means behaving oddly, so these letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor behaved oddly, and so gave everyone something to talk about.
explanation.definitionFit: A short amusing tale about a real incident is a story worth telling.

clue.text: Plant chief having slate put on .ramshackle huts

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman chief or commander
to pan is to criticise harshly, to slate

indicators.note: a ramshackle building is tumbledown, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boss with a slate roof puts it on some tumbledown huts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slate' looks like roofing but is the verb, to criticise; the stray dot in the text was a mark on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: African lily is a common name for this blue-flowered garden plant.

clue.text: In which there's loot, might you say?

definitions.text: In which there's loot, might you say?

parts.words: In which there's loot, might you say?
parts.note: a hidden store of stolen goods, whose name sounds like a word for money

explanation.surface: A question about where the stolen goods are stashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a secret hoard sounds just like a word for money, which is the loot.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret hoard of valuables or supplies is kept hidden in a stash.

clue.text: Big rock table with bolt right at the front

indicators.note: bolt and right are placed before the table, at its front

parts.note: a gib is a metal wedge or pin used to hold machine parts
an altar is a communion table

explanation.surface: A large stone slab with a bolt fixed on its right-hand front edge.
explanation.walkthrough: A gib is an engineering wedge or bolt. 'Big rock' is the nickname of the Rock of Gibraltar, the British territory off Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rock of Gibraltar, a huge limestone promontory, is popularly called the Rock.

clue.text: A lady gets ledge put up for plant

parts.note: Mary is a woman's name

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting up means reading upwards, so this word runs backwards

parts.note: a sill is a window ledge

explanation.surface: A woman gets a shelf raised to hold her potted plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns SILL into LLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The belladonna lily and the potted hippeastrum are both sold as this bulbous flowering plant.

clue.text: Meat and drink the high point either side of street

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: the high point sits on either side of street, so street goes within it

parts.note: a peak is a high point

explanation.surface: A menu of beef, spirits and a mountaintop view on each side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef from the hindquarters is a kind of meat.

clue.text: One hoping to make money from site finds solution in photographic business

definitions.text: One hoping to make money from site
definitions.meaning: a property speculator who builds on land
the chemical bath that brings out a film's image

explanation.surface: A property speculator finds an answer in the photography trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' looks like an answer but is a chemical liquid used in film processing.
explanation.definitionFit: A property builder profits from land; in darkrooms the same word names the chemical that reveals images.

clue.text: Fierce knight embraced by shrinking lady?

indicators.note: something embraced is held within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a shrinking violet is a shy person, and Violet a lady's name
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A shy woman is hugged by a fierce knight.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shrinking violet' is a timid person, so the shrinking lady is VIOLET; N is knight in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage and aggressive behaviour is described as fierce.

clue.text: Book compiled by gangster, dissolute type

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster
a bum is a loafer or idle, dissolute person

explanation.surface: A book written by a mobster, a rogue himself.
explanation.walkthrough: AL is the crossword's stock gangster, after Al Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound volume for photos or stamps is a kind of book.

clue.text: British soldiers on the way up showing weariness

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading upwards, so this word runs backwards

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner

explanation.surface: British troops marching uphill show signs of fatigue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MODE into EDOM. OR stands for other ranks, i.e. ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium and listlessness, a sense of being tired of everything, is a form of weariness.

clue.text: Show contempt for pain that's increasing

parts.note: to boo is to jeer and show contempt
a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a sore that keeps growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising or augmenting something is a synonym for increasing.

clue.text: Broom may lurk in wardrobe sometimes

indicators.note: something lurking in these words sits concealed within them, so the letters are taken from inside

explanation.surface: A broom might be found tucked away in the wardrobe now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional brush of twigs bound to a handle is an old-style broom.

clue.text: Indication that it's freezing for a time?

definitions.text: Indication that it's freezing for a time?

parts.words: Indication that it's freezing for a time?
parts.note: a thermometer reading of zero degrees could be written as a short word for temperature followed by a nought, and together these spell a musical word for pace

explanation.surface: A forecast-style question about the cold setting in for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: TEMP is short for temperature and O stands for zero; run together they give a word meaning a time or speed in music.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the speed at which a piece is played is its time or pace.

clue.text: Island seen as a pawn when grabbed by Persian king

indicators.note: something grabbed is held inside the grabber, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Cyrus the Great founded the Persian empire
P is chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A small island is treated as a pawn, seized by an ancient Persian ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: P is pawn in chess notation; CYRUS the Great was the founder of the Persian empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The eastern Mediterranean nation is an island.

clue.text: After first hint of sloth look lively

indicators.note: the word for look comes after the first letter of sloth
a first hint of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to pry is to look nosily

explanation.surface: Once the first sign of laziness passes, someone looks livelier.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble and active, especially for an older person, means lively.

clue.text: Vessel tips-shame asea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship tips over, a disgrace out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the ship picture but signals the shuffle of TIPS SHAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat driven by steam engines is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Accommodate 500 in part of theatre

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as the word says

parts.note: a loge is a box or section of seats in a theatre
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A theatre must find room for five hundred people in one section.
explanation.walkthrough: A loge is a theatre box; D is 500 in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To house or give someone a room is to put them up, a synonym for accommodate.

clue.text: Ways in which spirits may absorb an overdose

indicators.note: a thing absorbing another takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: meths, methylated spirits, is the British name for denatured alcohol

explanation.surface: How drink can take in a fatal dose, spirits and overdoses together.
explanation.walkthrough: METHS is British shorthand for methylated spirits, a denatured alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Techniques or procedures are ways of doing things.

clue.text: It gives Muslim women a narrow outlook

definitions.text: It gives Muslim women a narrow outlook

parts.words: It gives Muslim women a narrow outlook
parts.note: not a narrow-minded view but a veil leaving only a slit for the eyes

explanation.surface: Sounds like a criticism of attitudes, but is literal about a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'narrow outlook' suggests narrow-mindedness; literally it is the slit through which a veiled woman sees.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil worn by some Muslim women in public covers all the face except the eyes.
